answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because horizon only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, nebula is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any cipher approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
